REVIEW-B-M4/M8 P1: CTE inlining/width bugs — chained NOT MATERIALIZED inlines stale clones; scalar-subquery width check has empty CTE scope
close_reason: Fixed + verified (67ae0461d + ae5285d8c + a91d258b0). M4: inline_not_materialized_ctes now expands already-collected CTEs into each new body (dependency-order/fixpoint), so chained NOT MATERIALIZED (b reads a) inlines transitively and a's random() re-evaluates per reference (=0 not 1). M8: scalar-subquery/row-value width check no longer under-counts a SELECT * operand over an outer CTE — SelectStructureResolver threads self.visible_ctes() (precise), rewrite_in_expr fails open on wildcard operands (no CTE scope). False 'returns 2 columns - expected 1' gone. Keepers not_materialized_chained_random_reevaluates_wpiq6 + scalar_subquery_width_sees_outer_cte_wpiq6, no regression on gh204/row_value tests. NOTE: M8 query then hits a SEPARATE interpreted-evaluator gap (eval_join_expr can't execute row-value subquery comparisons) = bd-t7oeo (filed).

title: B2: Eliminate scan-per-row execution for IN and EXISTS subqueries
close_reason: Scan-per-row catastrophe fully resolved. IN subquery: 2885x→2.34x at 100K rows (F=0.016ms). EXISTS: faster than C SQLite (0.35x). All 23 regression tests pass. Residual 2-4x gap is fixed-cost MVCC overhead (~8us), not algorithmic.
